verdict.tagline: Action-packed co-op shooting that overcomes rough translation and matchmaking hurdles.
for_you_if: you enjoy cooperative rogue-lite shooting mechanics
you want deep character build variety
you can look past clunky tooltips
not_for_you_if: you rely heavily on public matchmaking

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players encounter frustrating control conflicts, poor translations, and heavy movement constraints.

claims.claim: The game features awkward or poor translation in ability and item descriptions, making them difficult to understand.

citations.review_text:
I think they used a machine translator or something because every line of text including descriptions of abilities and pickups are so difficult to read. Descriptions are things like "When Vigor >>60, can CostAllVigour to enter [Fist Stance]", or "If the quality of [Astrohouse] for [Falling Star] is not lower than last time, +20% DMG for every slot. If [Astrohouse] is the same as last time, +30% additional total DMG". One time I even saw a line of untranslated Chinese text.

The gameplay doesn't seem much better. It was cool for about 20 minutes but then I got sick of how repetitive it is. You basically just hold down left click with whatever weapon you feel like using. It seems like almost every character ability is essentially "Throw a ball. When it lands, it does AoE damage and maybe something else". Most attacks are just dodged by not holding still, but sometimes you get really telegraphed attacks that want you to press the dodge key which has a really long cooldown.

Maybe it gets better later, but I don't want to keep playing to find out. The weird translation definitely isn't going to get better.

great game overall very unique and fun weapon fun ability and skill tree for each hero couple downside are the enemy pathing which seem a lil buggy and the ability and scroll description over complicating stuff but that just minor thing compared to the good side recomend

The game is good, but it has issues. The biggest I'd say is, there are a fair amount of characters you can unlock by playing the game, either through levels or using the same resource used to get both general and character specific bonuses, BUT there are significantly more that are just bought with real money, and to my understanding that is the *only* way to get those characters.

Following that, the English translation isn't great. It's by no means unbearable, but you'll definitely notice, and it can make some skills harder to understand. But it's not that big a deal, it's mostly just funny when things are worded weirdly and a little off putting when item descriptions just don't look like they should. (I can't really explain that part, but it's just a bit off, still fine overall though)

Lastly, dodging is just odd. You go almost no where and I'm unsure if it has i-frames, plus it's on a cooldown, so it's just awkward to use and you'll probably end up dying when you feel you shouldn't have. This mixes horribly with the game kind of feeling like you're on above average ping even when playing solo. but that could just have been an adjustment issue.

Beyond those things though, which can mostly be ignored (or probably even worked around if you're bilingual, I'm not so I didn't check if swapping the language is any better), the game is just good. There's tons of weapons, a lot of characters (even if many are pay walled), and the general gunplay when it's working right is great. I do recommend it if you like rougelites and FPSs. Like I saw someone else say, it's pretty close to a first person Risk of Rain, though characters aren't nearly as diverse (same starting gun for everyone and many skills/grenades do seem to fall into just being damage or DoT, but there's elemental affinities for some and some do have very unique skills)

The gameplay loop seems fun, I can't lie. I'm sure that if I had a greater amount of patience for this game, I'd really like it. Having said that;

The items and weapons in the game have extremely obtuse descriptions, likely due to the less-than-fantastic translation/writing job. I came across [Efficient Firepower], a common-grade upgrade that reads as follows: 

"50% chance to get 1 extra recovery time when the secondary skill use < 50%; +60% secondary skill DMG when secondary skill use ≥ 50%". 

This seems extremely overwhelming until you realise it boils down to: 
"50% chance to restore 1 Secondary charge if below half. Otherwise, +60% Secondary damage."

Additionally, the very first boss of the game, Lu Wu, seems extremely unforgiving. Not particularly challenging, I didn't struggle too much with him, but his AoE attacks were immensely hard to dodge as a player who wasn't expecting them and often plays games of this kind. I'm quite confident in my adaptability but it felt like a lot of attacks Lu Wu threw at me were bizarrely hard to avoid.

The above issues aren't so bad on paper, but when you consider that none of this can be solved by community efforts due to the developers' anti-modding stance - especially the overcomplication on weapon traits and upgrade descriptions - learning the gameplay loop feels more like studying for a test between rooms than growing in power during a run.

I really enjoyed this game's loop for the 40 minutes that I played it, though. The gunplay felt fluid and fun, the weapons and effects were enjoyable to use and I really like the aesthetic of the game. If these things sound cool to you and the above issue(s) don't bother you at all, absolutely try this game out, but I can't personally recommend it after the time I've spent with it.

claims.claim: The game exhibits input issues when a controller is plugged in, refusing to recognize mouse and keyboard inputs.

citations.review_text:
Load up the game, stuck on "2025 Roadmap" prompting for a controller input. I don't have a controller connected or anywhere near my PC. It wont recognize any mouse or keyboard inputs.

This is an extremely embarassing intro experience to a game.

7 minutes in

-First thing you see is an ad for a season pass, in a game I paid 10 bucks for
-Tutorial is a glorified QTE where you have no freedom
-Tutorial unironically has the text "Hint: hold W to move forward" and "Hint: keep going" on the screen
-Once the tutorial is over, they show you regular menus but force you to click one specific button and start a new run. First time I see this outside of those legalized scams called gachas
-Tried adjusting settings, couldn't even adjust my crosshair because the game locked my mouse cursor at the center of the screen and I couldn't do anything, had to Alt F4
-Upon restarting the game would literally refuse to take mouse and keyboard inputs simply because I have a controller plugged in

I'll probably keep going because I know I'll enjoy the gameplay but this ♥♥♥♥ is inexcusable. Especially forcing me to unplug my controller to use m+k, genuinely what the ♥♥♥♥ kinda design is that

EDIT 10 minutes later: Actually after reading a bunch of negative reviews I'm not even gonna bother lmao

claims.claim: Players report difficulty finding other people to play with through the co-op matchmaking system.

citations.review_text: I am quite enjoying this game, but it’s very unfortunate that I can’t find anyone during matchmaking to play co-op.

I really enjoyed Abyssus so I ended up grabbing this game to see if I could scratch that itch. Abyssus has a great style and gunplay and I thought Gunfire Reborn just wouldn't be able to replicate it. Well, it cant, but it certainly has its own charm. What Gunfire Reborn really does well is the sheer amount of content. It's been around for years and apparently has received constant development, even though I was not able to find a multiplayer game despite trying to.

I have barely scratched the surface of the content in this game, but in Abyssus after 15 hours I had 70% of all the unlocks and achievements, and had maxed the difficulty into infinite scaling.

This game doesn't quite feel as rewarding but there are more zones and bosses which already is a huge plus. There's also a lot more strategic depth with the increased number of characters and their interactions with various weapons and elements. But I also think the game really doesn't do certain playstyles very well at all, like weapon switching. The way the game is set up is not accommodating to multi weapon builds at all, despite so many scrolls being exactly for that. It ends up being useful to some heroes, but I could see the counterintuitive design immediately.

It, despite being much older, also lacks the polish of Abyssus. While there is so much more content, I wouldn't say it is of higher quality. Ultimately it runs into the same issues as the other game, just a little later with a bit more grinding. The game is a little stingy with soul fragments, the meta currency for talent points in Gunfire Reborn. I am well aware at some point you will just have the whole tree unlocked. But it feels really bad to spend a whole match earning only enough fragments for 1 or 2 talent points.

I would say the game has promise, and a future. It's fun, addictive in a way, and a breath of fresh air after playing a game in the same genre. The heroes especially keep things fresh, but some heroes are definitely more f…

claims.claim: The game runs laggy when a large amount of enemies are nearby, even when playing on lower graphics settings.

citations.review_text:
It's always a pleasure when actual art comes out of China. It's all too common to see Chinese games that are lazy, use AI generation, lazily taking other games' ideas, stuffed with microtransactions... When something like this comes along, it really feels good to be able to just enjoy the game as a quality product.

Gunfire Reborn is a charming roguelite looter shooter. You pick your character out of several unique heroes who all have different playstyles. Some very different, but a decent variety nonetheless. You then fight your way through first person shooter arenas. When conquering each arena, you're typically given a choice of power ups to augment your playstyle. There are different types of powerups you can get, from items that give you more gold to augments to your character's fundamental abilities.

The gameplay is buttery smooth, well optimized and has never crashed on me. The gamefeel is so natural that I've watched a 6 year old play this game. He didn't get too far but he had a great time.

I can't really say anything stands out remarkably. The artstyle is probably the most notable aspect, with every character and enemy being some anthropomophized animal. Thankfully, nothing is sexualized and the animals aren't TOO human. It doesn't come across as some weirdo furry's fetish that he's sticking in everyone else's face. The artstyle is cute, charming, and does a great job of depicting the characters. In particular, you can tell exactly who characters like Ao Bai are just by looking at them. A tough and no nonsense fellow.

Ultimately this game is an easy recommend if you like FPS games. An absolutely astounding array of weird and whacky weapons (you can just grab a dragon and that's your gun. It's a flamethrower) make replays a pleasure. Characters aren't typically locked in to a type of weapon that they have to use, but rather they get bonuses that work alongside the weapons. Dashes, crowd control, elemental effects, dual wield and other powers make up the …

its simple and fun even if its repetitive. i enjoy the smooth tracking aspect without the stress of the enemies being hard to track/kill. i did find it to be laggy when a large amount of enemies are nearby despite being on lower graphics

citations.review_text:
+ Very fun weapons, I really have to emphasize this, no other game has done something like this one has
+ Most weapons (not explosive) can headshot (including weird ones like one that expands a ring out from you)
+ Fun progression
+ No FOMO (you can buy previous season rewards with the same currency for level up, no MTX) 
+ Decently high skill expression
+ Game will allow you to break it in fun ways (crazy crit multipliers, damage resistance stacking)
+ Most characters are interesting gameplay wise (Not the vanilla/starter one)
+ Optimized enough to give stable 144 fps

? Grindy (fun kind of grindy but still grindy)
? Longish runs (~30 minutes if I ignore vaults/extras, 90min+ on elite mode)

- Game encourages you to dump everything into upgrading a single weapon
- Very bad writing for weapon descriptions. Can be confusing, luckily someone has improved the translation on Nexus Mods as a custom translation file (csv)
- BS DPS check final boss
- Bad movement system. Feels extremely slow until later on
- very early on (first 5ish runs) you will die to stuff that's not your fault

Solid roguelite shooter with a variety of unique weapons from traditional assault rifles to black-hole launchers to a lizard that shoots fire, each with their own unique gimmick so that even two guns in the same class can play wildly differently, as well as a number of different characters with skills that support multiple playstyles and builds allowing for a ton of replayability. Allows up to 4 players to go together, with a wealth of difficulty options to fine-tune your experience. Has season-based additions that can be swapped to at any time to further diversify buildcrafting, as well as fairly regular updates adding more free content and paid DLC characters. base game is dirt cheap for what you get, too, and even after a season ends you can still access the content it added.

There are some problems, like the localization not always being the best; there's effects that are way too wordy and hard to understand, and in some cases might not even show up in your selected language. There's bugs, and sometimes when connecting to another player the ping will be absurdly high even if the two players are in the same region. But for a game so cheap, I'm willing to overlook minor issues like this.

And also it involves a bunch of cute animal characters which is always a plus.

I feel like I'm taking crazy pills with all the positive reviews toward this game.

Before I come across like a raving lunatic, I wanna say that the best part of this game is the multiplayer and if that's what you're interested in, then play Risk of Rain 2 instead. But, on the off-chance that you've already played Risk of Rain 2, then play Risk of Rain Returns instead. If you've played them both, then maybe Gunfire Reborn is worth a try, though Windblown is pretty fun so far too.

This game is extremely flat. You're given so many build-defining choices throughout a run that it's extremely easy to hone in on exactly what you want every single time. This means replay value is entirely self-motivated but once you find a functional build, there's little to discourage you from pursuing it every single time.

You're given so many item drops that sorting through them is nightmarish and the horrible translations make it even more cumbersome. Just figuring out what a skill does often involves reading, rereading, testing, and then checking an external wiki just to make sense of it and it's not entirely uncommon for power-ups to contain a literal paragraph of descriptive text in barely-functional English.

If you can make it past the first 15 minutes of a run, you are almost guaranteed to win because there are so many layers of defense in this game that becoming functionally immortal is the natural result of spending enough time opening chests. At the same time, the first 15 minutes can often result in you being mysteriously one-shot and kicked back to the start.

The game incorporates Seasonal mechanics which are also poorly explained and usually require you to read paragraphs upon paragraphs of conditional effects in order to make use of them.

This game is straight-up decent but I wouldn't recommend it for all the above reasons and also the undisclosed AI art is kind of a bummer. The deer girl is extremely hot.

The best RoR2 adjacent game, been absolutely obsessed since buying it around a week ago. 
tight gunplay, interesting items, EXTREMELY creative weapons. try to buy all the dlc, you don't want to miss out on any of the crazy weapons in this game.

my only gripe is the music is a bit uninspired, but you'll probably be blasting your own tunes before long in these types of games anyway. that and the translation is quite bad in places, reading what something does can be confusing because of this, but the wiki helps clear up any confusion. 

still receiving regular dlc/free seasonal content as of this post!

Not a bad game. Gunplay feels fun enough, gameplay is intuitive but I've seen it before, some descriptions on occult scrolls are a little vague and I often find myself looking at the wiki trying to figure out if it's good or not. Other than that, this is a pretty fun game. Pretty sure the people dogging on this game rn are just finding some excuse to hate on it. It has flaws, but it's still a pretty fun game.

This game is Borderlands for roguelite fans, fast paced and fairly difficult, it also has hundreds of guns to explore.

A few negatives though:
- Translation is rough in some parts in English.
- There's only 4 environments
- Enemy variety is just OK, it gets interesting on the very last act.

Gunplay is fun and satisfying, hell just look at my playtime. Unfortunately:
- Build variety kind of sucks. Pretty much every character has the exact same 3 builds (weapon, secondary skill, primary skill) with the only differences being what weapon type your character wants to use. After a while it gets VERY stale. Seasonal mechanics are basically identical to each other in terms of buffs and mechanics so the game has next to nothing to shake up the gameplay.

- In-game text is very obviously machine translated. Lots of skill and item/scroll descriptions are borderline nonsensical, with inconsistent terminology and straight-up incorrect descriptions. There is also just a lot of entirely untranslated text that sneaks its way into the game every update.

- DLC power creep is very much a thing. Paid characters are much, much better than base-game characters and it is almost impossible to lose a run with them, even on the highest difficulty.

- Performance and other issues: game has been running worse and worse the longer it's out and this isn't being addressed at all - there has been at least one documented case of a player getting a virus partially due to the game pinging a domain the developers no longer have access to. (potential false-positive, but worth mentioning.)

- UNDISCLOSED GENAI USAGE. GenAI is being used to create both promotional comics seen in the news updates for the game as well as for animated in-game emotes unlocked via the battle pass.
The developers use generative AI slop for official artwork and emotes. Avoid.
Newest batch of dlc + comics about the new dlc are made using Ai image generation. Like the dev is a fascist AND hates artists? Putrid.

I like the game because it has dozens of builds to experiment with and they all have incredibly unique playstyles. It has simple and amazing graphics. The characters with their builds are pretty straightforward and they can go way further in unexpected ways that work. This game has almost infinite possibilities and outcomes! The only downside me and my friends found is that after hundreds of hours dedicated in this game, it just becomes incredibly repetitive which kind of ruins the fun in this underrated roguelike game after some time. Also, please fix the languages that are Chinese letters by default to the ones we have selected in the settings because everytime I see that, I have to decrypt them using google translate everytime lol. In summary, this game is amazing with little downsides. One of my favorite games.

Pretty much every character has the exact same 3 builds (weapon, secondary skill, primary skill) with the only differences being what weapon type your character wants to use. After a while it gets VERY stale. Seasonal mechanics are basically identical to each other in terms of buffs and mechanics so the game has next to nothing to shake up the gameplay.

- In-game text is very obviously machine translated. Lots of skill and item/scroll descriptions are borderline nonsensical, with inconsistent terminology and straight-up incorrect descriptions. There is also just a lot of entirely untranslated text that sneaks its way into the game every update.

- DLC power creep is very much a thing. Paid characters are much, much better than base-game characters and it is almost impossible to lose a run with them, even on the highest difficulty.

- Performance and other issues: game has been running worse and worse the longer it's out and this isn't being addressed at all - there has been at least one documented case of a player getting a virus partially due to the game pinging a domain the developers no longer have access to. (potential false-positive, but worth mentioning.)

- UNDISCLOSED GENAI USAGE. GenAI is being used to create both promotional comics seen in the news updates for the game as well as for animated in-game emotes unlocked via the battle pass.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience performance issues with random frame drops, lag spikes, and stutters following recent updates.

citations.review_text: Decided to give this game a go after a long time of not playing. Discovered performance has never been worse. Terrible stutters. I remember i liked this game a lot because it ran incredibly well, felt snappy and precise, now its stutterfest.

The game is great in terms of gameplay, replayability, and art style. It used to run smoothly on my device, but after in recent updates, it became difficult to run even on the lowest graphics settings. The game now has random frame drops and lag spikes. I really love this game, and I hope the developers optimize it so I can enjoy playing again without having to lower the graphics too much.
